title: Why a Moving Bus Looks Still Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
Sit in a train and the train beside you seems to stand still. Stand on the platform and the same train rushes past. Which is true? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (Chapter 2, Motion in a Straight Line) we learn relative velocity in one dimension and solve every such puzzle with one subtraction.

You will watch two buses on a live simulation, first from the ground and then from inside bus A, with a position-time graph that changes as the view changes, and a slow-motion replay when bus B turns around. We derive v_BA = v_B - v_A step by step, show why v_AB = -v_BA, and use parallel lines on an x-t graph to explain why a bus beside you looks frozen. Two pause-and-think questions test closing speed and crossing lines. Then a worked overtaking example, the exam trap about signs, an original JEE Main / NEET pattern question on crossing trains with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 One train, two views
0:28 What is relative velocity?
0:47 Two buses: ground view vs the view from bus A
1:32 The rule, step by step
2:14 Why a bus beside you looks frozen
2:40 Same way vs opposite ways + pause and think
3:32 Worked example: when does the car catch up?
4:09 Exam trap: forgetting the sign
4:31 Practice question (JEE Main / NEET pattern)
5:11 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Scalars and Vectors, the first topic of Chapter 3. Five newtons plus five newtons can give ten newtons, or zero. How?
